name: Systems Analyst and IT Manager
description: ⚠⚠⚠ Computer and information systems managers earn $175,140 with 55,600 openings a year — and 26% of them report reaching it with SOME COLLEGE AND NO DEGREE, against 48% with a bachelor's and 14% with a master's. ⚠⚠ The rung below, computer systems analyst, is $105,850 across 521,100 jobs. This is the best-paid management occupation on the site and one of the most credential-loose.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ THE CREDENTIAL REQUIREMENT LOOSENS AS THE PAY RISES, WHICH IS BACKWARDS AND WORTH UNDERSTANDING. O*NET's employer data for computer and information systems managers — the $175,140 job — reports 48% bachelor's, 26% SOME COLLEGE AND NO DEGREE, and 14% master's. ⚠ Nothing in this family is licensed, there is no required major, and no professional body gatekeeps entry. ⚠⚠ What that means in practice: the degree gets you interviewed early in a career and demonstrated delivery gets you promoted after that, so a degree is worth buying at the start and rarely worth buying later. A master's is the least useful purchase on this page unless you are moving into a specialism that names it. ⚠⚠ THE CERTIFICATIONS THAT DO GET NAMED are vendor and framework ones — cloud platform certifications, project management (PMP), ITIL, security credentials such as Security+ or CISSP for the governance track. They are cheap relative to a degree, they expire, and they are what a mid-career candidate without a degree uses to prove currency. ⚠ Ask any employer which ones they actually screen on, because the list is short and it changes.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The pay rises and the credential requirement falls

RoleSOC2025 medianEmployedOpenings/yrGrowth 2024–34Entry
Computer systems analyst15-1211$105,850521,10034,200✅ much faster (7%+)bachelor's, associate or some college
✅✅ Computer and information systems manager11-3021✅✅ $175,140✅ 667,100✅ 55,600✅ much faster (7%+)⚠⚠ 48% bachelor's, 26% SOME COLLEGE, 14% master's

⚠⚠⚠ $175,140, and a quarter of the people earning it never finished a degree. That is the highest median of any management occupation on this site and one of the loosest credential profiles on it.

⚠⚠ The honest reading is not “skip the degree”. It is that the degree buys the first interview and delivery buys everything after it — so it is worth paying for at the start of a career and rarely worth paying for later. The 26% did not skip the work; they substituted fifteen years of it.

⚠ And note the scale. 667,100 managers with 55,600 openings a year is a very large management occupation — more people manage information systems in the United States than work as registered nurses in Florida, several times over.

⚠⚠ MIS or computer science? It is a question about placement, not content

Management information systemsComputer science
Sits inthe business schoolthe computing school
FL public institutions1316
Aims atdeciding what gets builtbuilding it
Typical first rolesystems analyst, $105,850software developer, $135,980
The rung above✅ IT manager, $175,140 — reached from both

⚠⚠⚠ Computer science pays about $30,000 more at the first rung; MIS points more directly at the rung above. Both routes reach the management job, and plenty of the 26% with no degree reached it from neither.

⚠ The test that actually decides it: do you want to write the code, or decide which code is worth writing? If it is the first, take computer science and do not let anyone tell you MIS is the easier path to the same place — the first rung is $30,000 apart.

⚠⚠ Worth knowing for access: Seminole State College awards 103 MIS bachelor's a year, fourth in the state behind USF, FAU and Florida State. A state college in the top four for a business-technology baccalaureate is unusual, and it means this degree is reachable without a university for students near Sanford.

⚠⚠ One subject, two course numbers, and no institution carries both

NumberCarriersSector
ISM3011 Introduction to Information Systems Management127 state colleges, 5 universities
ISM4011 Introduction to Management Information Systems109 state colleges, 1 university
⚠⚠⚠ Overlap: none. Not one Florida public institution carries both.

⚠⚠ This is NOT the trap the marketing pages carry. There, MAR2011 is lower division and MAR3023 upper, so the cheaper one cannot supply baccalaureate hours. Here both numbers are upper division, so no credit is lost whichever you take.

⚠ The risk is purely transfer matching: an evaluator comparing ISM3011 against ISM4011 sees two different numbers and may not recognise them as the same course. Send the syllabus, not the number — it is a one-line problem that costs a semester if you leave it to the evaluator.

⚠ Security lives inside this curriculum too

ISM4323 Information Systems Security is carried by 10 Florida institutions and ISM4324 Cybersecurity Analytics by 6 — inside the business prefix, not the computing one.

⚠⚠ That is the governance and risk half of security: policy, compliance, audit, risk assessment, incident response management. It is a different job from the technical security work on this site's cybersecurity path, it pays comparably, and it is reached from a business degree. If the organisational side of security interests you more than the packet captures, this is the route.

⚠ And the analytical end has already moved: ISM4545 Advanced Machine Learning for Business is carried by six Florida institutions, in the business prefix. MIS is not the non-technical option it was fifteen years ago.

Necessary skills

  • Requirements elicitation. Getting people who cannot describe their own process to describe their own process is the analyst's core skill and the hardest to fake.
  • Systems analysis and design as a formal discipline — ISM3113 and ISM4113 exist for it at seven and six institutions.
  • Enough technical depth to be lied to and notice. You will commission work you cannot do yourself.
  • Project management. ISM4314 is carried by seven institutions, and the PMP is the credential most often named in postings.
  • Writing a business case — cost, benefit, risk, and what happens if nothing is done.
  • Databases and data modelling, because almost every organisational system is a database with opinions attached.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Buy the degree at the start, not later. 26% of the people in the $175,140 job have no degree, but essentially all of them substituted a long career for it. If you are 19, the bachelor's is the cheap route; if you are 40 and already in the industry, certifications and delivery are.

⚠⚠ Decide MIS against computer science on what you want to do, not on which is easier. The first rung differs by about $30,000 in computer science's favour; the management rung above is common to both.

⚠ Take systems analysis and project management seriously. They are the two courses that describe the actual job, and they are what distinguishes an analyst from a graduate who can only code a little.

⚠ If you transfer, send the syllabus for your intro course. ISM3011 and ISM4011 are the same subject and no institution carries both, so the receiving evaluator has probably never seen the other one.

And look at Seminole State if a university is not convenient. 103 bachelor's a year puts it fourth in Florida for this degree, at state-college prices.

programs.note: The named degree — 13 Florida public institutions, 735 credentials, 628 of them bachelor's. USF 183, FAU 159, Florida State 148, ⚠ Seminole State College 103. Read its degrees note on the ISM3011 / ISM4011 numbering split.

⚠⚠⚠ The comparison to make, and it is about placement rather than content: computing school against business school, building against deciding what to build. ⚠ Software developers earn $135,980 against systems analysts' $105,850 — about $30,000 at the first rung — while the management job above pays $175,140 and is reached from both.

⚠⚠ Much more widely taught — 39 Florida institutions against 13 — and the operational rather than analytical route. IT runs the systems; MIS specifies them. ⚠ If a degree near home matters more than the specific title, IT is far more available.

⚠ A real overlap: ISM4323 Information Systems Security is carried by 10 Florida institutions and ISM4324 Cybersecurity Analytics by 6, inside the BUSINESS prefix. ⚠⚠ That is the governance, risk and compliance half of security, and it is reached from this degree rather than from a computing one.

⚠⚠ Where the analytical end has gone — ISM4545 Advanced Machine Learning for Business is already carried by six Florida institutions in the business prefix. ⚠ If the modelling rather than the management is the draw, look there before committing here.
⚠ The parent field: an MIS degree is a business degree with a technology concentration, and general business with information systems coursework reaches many of the same jobs from more institutions.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Introduction to Information Systems Management — 12 Florida institutions (7 state colleges, 5 universities). The gateway course of the degree.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ Florida carries the same subject as ISM4011 at 10 other institutions, and NO institution carries both. Both are upper division so no credit is lost — but a transfer evaluator matching numbers will not recognise them as the same course. Send the syllabus.

courses.reason: Introduction to Management Information Systems — 10 Florida institutions (9 state colleges, 1 university). The same subject under the other number.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Zero overlap with ISM3011's carriers. Whichever your institution uses is the right one; the problem only appears on transfer.

courses.reason: ⚠⚠ Information Systems Security — 10 institutions, the most widely carried upper-division ISM course after the introductions. The governance and risk half of security, taught in the business school.
Business Data Communications — 9 institutions. Networking from the business side: what the infrastructure costs, what it enables and what it risks.
⚠ Systems Analysis and Design — 7 institutions. The course that describes the actual job of a systems analyst, and the one that separates an analyst from someone who can code a little.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also numbered ISM4113 Analysis and Design of Business Information Systems at 6 institutions — the same subject again under a second number. Register by number.

courses.reason: ⚠ Project Management — 7 institutions. The PMP is the credential most often named in postings for this family, and this is where Florida teaches the underlying discipline.
Database Design and Administration — 6 institutions. Almost every organisational system is a database with opinions attached, and data modelling is the durable skill.
Cybersecurity Analytics — 6 institutions. The measurement side of security governance, and a good signal that a programme takes the risk track seriously.

⚠ Advanced Machine Learning for Business — 6 institutions. Named to correct a stale impression: MIS is not the non-technical option it was, and the analytical content is now inside the business prefix.
Introduction to programming — named because an analyst who cannot read code is at the mercy of the people who write it. ⚠ You do not need to be a developer; you do need to be able to follow one.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers introductory programming several ways (COP1000, COP2000, COP2224, COP2220, CGS1540). Any of them serves.

courses.reason: Financial Accounting — 32 institutions. A business case is an accounting document, and the analyst who writes one that survives finance is the one whose projects get funded.
Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Required for the degree, and the analytics content above assumes it.
Principles of Management — 17 institutions. Named because the destination on this page is a management job, and 55,600 of them open a year.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Requirements documents, business cases and incident reports are the analyst's output, and ambiguity in them is expensive.
Fundamentals of Speech Communication — 16 institutions. Requirements elicitation is an interview, and presenting a business case is a performance. Both are teachable.
